title: Bind Skill approval to a typed Skill identity
goal: Make policy and approval boundaries receive the exact Skill ID as structured ActionIntent data instead of relying on parsing a free-form summary.
context: M6 currently constructs ActionIntent without skillID, so an ApprovalGate cannot identify which Skill it is authorizing. M6ApprovedSkillPolicy also identifies the Skill by exact summary-string matching rather than a typed field.
forbidden_changes: Do not make skillID mandatory for existing non-Skill ActionIntent callers.
Do not weaken policy or approval checks.
Do not identify Skills by parsing free-form summary text when a typed ID is available.
acceptance_criteria: ActionIntent has an optional typed skillID field while existing non-Skill call sites remain source-compatible.
M6 passes proposal.skillID into the policy and approval boundary.
SkillRuntime passes its requested Skill ID into its policy boundary.
M6ApprovedSkillPolicy validates the typed skillID rather than parsing summary text.
Regression proves ApprovalGate receives the exact requested skillID and no toolID for a Skill proposal.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: Keep the field optional and source-compatible, thread exact Skill identity through M6 and SkillRuntime, and retain all existing fail-closed capability checks.
